readerContract.humanQuestion: Which part of an AI-written personal message needs checking before I send it?
readerContract.promisedPayoff: Spot a factual addition inside polished wording and know what source could support it.
readerContract.priorKnowledge: Adult beginner, no AI vocabulary or film knowledge required.
readerContract.centralMentalModel: Drafting wording does not establish the truth of the claims inside it.
readerContract.dailyLifeConnection: A message arranging dinner and a note about a delivery.
readerContract.surfaceJob: One original episode quote, one small think-and-reveal challenge and a source link.
readerContract.desiredFeeling: Amused, alert and able to check a concrete detail.

canonicalTruth.freshnessTrigger: Episode wording or published route changes; no current product-specific promises.

strengthsToUse: Familiar human question and bounded task
Earned humour and a useful next action

candidateRepairNotes: First Overheard pilot. Keep accepted source wording exact. A draft can contain claims; do not present them as exclusive output types.

draftArchitecture.plainAnswer: The claimed booking time needs checking against the confirmation; fluent wording is not proof of a booking.
causalSequence: Reader sees an original source quote.
A hypothetical draft adds a precise booking time.
Reveal identifies the claim and the external evidence needed.
A second delivery example lets the reader transfer the distinction.
draftArchitecture.workedCase: Dinner invitation draft says booking is at7 when no time was supplied.
draftArchitecture.transferCase: Delivery message says parcel has shipped; check actual tracking or dispatch confirmation.
draftArchitecture.usefulAction: Before sending an AI-written message, check added factual details against their source.
draftArchitecture.formatSpecificStructure: Compact newspaper insert with one details reveal and source button; no account, collection, fake score or timer.
draftArchitecture.antiTemplateDecision: One short interaction, not another full lesson or repeated card grid.

analogyPlan.concept: Draft wording versus supported factual claim
analogyPlan.mapping: An outfit concerns presentation; an alibi needs evidence.
analogyPlan.limit: A draft can contain claims; metaphor is followed by concrete checking and never substitutes for it.
analogyPlan.whyItHelps: A concise original joke makes the distinction memorable.

humourPlan.lessonJob: The original source quote sets up the distinction; mock formality may support the reveal without another pop-culture reference.

communicationDesign.surfaceAdaptation: One short optional reveal with an ordinary personal-life example; do not imitate a science presenter.

representativeProofPlan.highestRisk: The joke obscures that claims can occur inside any draft, or a guessed booking time is treated as verified.
representativeProofPlan.plannedProof: Read exact short copy and reveal in full; independently solve the dinner challenge and transfer; browser keyboard and narrow-layout check.
representativeProofPlan.acceptanceOutcome: Reader can identify the unsupported time and name the actual confirmation needed; source link works and reveal is accessible.
